description: Project NOAH (Nationwide Operational Assessment of Hazards) produced national hazard maps for the Philippines, and the BetterGov.ph open data portal republishes them as one cloud-optimised file. The dataset page read on 2026-09-28 describes a collection of geospatial hazard assessments covering flood, landslide (including debris flow) and storm surge hazard zones across the Philippines, published under the Department of Science and Technology, offered as a single 5.17 GB PMTiles vector tile resource derived from the Project NOAH shapefiles for direct use in web maps, last updated on 11 April 2026 and licensed under the Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL). Coverage is national. Access is free download. Caveats: BetterGov.ph is a civic repackaging, so the original NOAH scenario definitions (return periods, storm surge advisories) must be checked against the source maps, and PMTiles need a tile-aware tool to convert back to features. It supports flood, landslide and storm surge exposure studies of roads, buildings and facilities in the Philippines. Related record: data-para-philippine-amateur-radio-repeaters lists emergency radio sites that can be overlaid on the hazard zones.
